llm.reply:
The condition identified across NCBI is Lynch syndrome [7]. Causal and associated genetic factors include mutL homolog 1 [10]. Additional key mismatch repair and associated genes include mutS homolog 2 [11].

## Genetic Architecture

The disorder involves mutS homolog 6 [8]. Pathogenesis is also linked to PMS1 homolog 2, mismatch repair system component [14]. Other implicated loci include epithelial cell adhesion molecule [9]. Genomic associations further include mutL homolog 3 [6].

## Associated Loci

The network includes PMS1 homolog 1, mismatch repair system component [13]. It further encompasses transforming growth factor beta receptor 2 [16]. Disease associations also involve neurofibromin 1 [12]. Additional linked loci comprise cadherin 1 [17].

## Clinical Studies

Active investigations include the study Implementation of a New Strategy to Identify HNPCC Patients [1]. Clinical evaluation is represented by Hereditary Nonpolyposis Colorectal Cancer in Taiwan-Related Genetic Study and Clinical Applications [2]. Counseling research includes Psychosocial Aspects of Genetic Testing for Hereditary Nonpolyposis Colon Cancer [3]. Patient registries include Registry for Women Who Are At Risk Or May Have Lynch Syndrome [5].

## Context And Literature

MedGen indexes the condition under the title Lynch syndrome [19]. Biomedical publications include the work indexed under pmid 21508689 [21]. Literature resources classify the entity as Colorectal Neoplasms Hereditary Nonpolyposis [23]. Clinical reviews also include the work under pmid 34798986 [29].

Lynch syndrome is characterized as a distinct hereditary cancer condition [7]. The disorder is cataloged as a disease under MedGen concept Lynch syndrome [19].

## Associated Genes

The condition links to multiple DNA mismatch repair and tumor-associated genes, including mutS homolog 2 [11]. It is also defined by mutL homolog 1 [10]. Additional mismatch repair factors include mutS homolog 6 [8]. The system further links mutL homolog 3 [6]. Another component is PMS1 homolog 1, mismatch repair system component [13]. Associated repair proteins also include PMS1 homolog 2, mismatch repair system component [14]. Cell-surface adhesion is represented by epithelial cell adhesion molecule [9]. Tumor suppression and cell adhesion are represented by cadherin 1 [17]. Growth factor signaling involves transforming growth factor beta receptor 2 [16]. Other implicated loci include neurofibromin 1 [12]. Cellular translation components also link ribosomal protein S20 [15].

## Clinical Trials

Clinical research includes Implementation of a New Strategy to Identify HNPCC Patients [1]. Geographic and translational studies include Hereditary Nonpolyposis Colorectal Cancer in Taiwan-Related Genetic Study and Clinical Applications [2]. Counseling-focused protocols include Psychosocial Aspects of Genetic Testing for Hereditary Nonpolyposis Colon Cancer [3]. Patient communication was investigated by Educational CD-ROM Compared With Standard Informed Consent for Patients With Colorectal Cancer or a Family History of Colorectal Cancer [4]. Longitudinal tracking includes Registry for Women Who Are At Risk Or May Have Lynch Syndrome [5].

## Literature Evidence

Literature indexing includes the entity term Lynch syndrome I (site-specific colonic cancer) [20]. Broader naming appears as Colorectal Neoplasms Hereditary Nonpolyposis [23]. Extracolonic disease is indexed as Lynch Syndrome II [26]. Foundational literature includes the article title Lynch syndrome. [18]. Comparative pathology is discussed in Differentiating Lynch-like from Lynch syndrome. [22]. Malignancy reviews include Lynch Syndrome-Associated Colorectal Cancer. [25]. Clinical screening is presented in Identification of Lynch Syndrome. [28]. Molecular management is detailed in Lynch Syndrome Genetics and Clinical Implications. [30]. Related citations include 21508689 [21]. Literature monitoring also includes 24468183 [24]. Diagnostic studies further cite 30134129 [27]. Genetic tracking is cited in 34798986 [29].
